Keep the yellow creature's anatomy, large green-ringed black eyes and small horizontal mouth; do not restore human skin, human nose or human ears. Express the original mood through its creature eyes and mouth plus retained eyebrows.
Facial-hair placement: wherever the original has a moustache and chin beard, their top-to-bottom order is eyes, UPPER-LIP moustache, small horizontal mouth, chin beard. Retain the visible shape, symbol count and arrangement of source collar patches and existing decorations. Do not invent chest medallions. Any source note markings that are illegible remain indistinct texture; do not invent readable serial numbers, identification codes, words or labels.

No neck clipping through collar, pinched narrow ring, floating collar, broken seam or abrupt geometric junction. The creamy belly stays under opaque clothing; never add a cream/white bib on the neck. Respect this fit even for tiny advisor or pilot portraits.
The head silhouette is nearly round or a SHORT egg shape. Its chin rests immediately above the garment collar, without copying the original human neck length. Preserve the shoulder position and crop by broadening the fitted garment; do not fill that space with a tall yellow column.
The garment meets the underside of a visibly rounded chin. There is no separate exposed vertical neck column between the head and collar, including bald and three-quarter-view portraits.

No comparison board, new text, label, watermark or extra figure.
